statements.statement: RTPSParticipant drives participant announcement through SPDP only after local transport locators are configured.
SPDP discovery of a new participant triggers SEDP endpoint announcements to the discovered participant metatraffic locator.
When a discovered participant lease expires, participant-level state removes that participant and endpoint matches are dissolved.
SEDP-discovered compatible reader/writer endpoints are wired into local StatefulWriter/StatefulReader match tables and unwired on participant removal.
RTPSParticipant initializes its own GUID with a participant EntityId and a platform-provided GuidPrefix.
Participant local address configuration updates SPDP metatraffic multicast locator selection and announce eligibility.
parse_received dispatches DATA to user readers addressed by readerId and fans out when readerId is UNKNOWN.
parse_received dispatches ACKNACK and NACK_FRAG submessages to the addressed local writer for reliability state processing.
An endpoint announced without unicast locators is reached at its participant's defaultUnicastLocatorList.
A local endpoint whose topic or type name exceeds RTPS_MAX_TOPIC_NAME_LEN - 1 is refused rather than announced under a truncated name.

Local addresses are added with their on-link prefix length; the participant sends to a peer at the announced locator inside that prefix ahead of the peer's other locators, and a removed address no longer ranks them.
When a discovered participant re-announces SPDP with new default or metatraffic unicast locators, user DATA, ACKNACKs and SEDP traffic to it use the new locators without a rematch.

Every announced participant is recorded, up to RTPS_MAX_KNOWN_PEERS; SEDP is exchanged with at most RTPS_MAX_PEERS of them. A peer finding that active tier full is admitted once a settled peer is parked for it, a parked peer's SPDP renews its lease, and a parked peer announcing a newer SEDP change is reactivated and its announcement processed.

A parked peer's lease is renewed without a full decode only by a PL_CDR payload whose PID_PARTICIPANT_GUID carries that peer's prefix; an empty, malformed, or foreign payload leaves the lease unchanged.

A peer is parked only when settled: its SEDP is fully received and acknowledged, no SEDP DATA from it within RTPS_PEER_SETTLE_MS, and none of its endpoints in a match except with the discovery writer; parking removes its builtin SEDP proxies and its remote endpoints.

A participant's user writers and readers bind proxies from two participant-wide pools. Every endpoint slot's floor is reserved from construction; a larger floor is reserved when the endpoint is created, which is refused when the pool cannot hold it; deleting an endpoint returns its proxies and its larger floor.

A match whose proxy the pool or the endpoint's cap refuses is kept waiting, not dropped, and keeps its peer in a match. After a proxy frees, each tick binds one waiting match, the oldest by the order the matches were reported among those that can bind; the bound endpoint starts it as a newly matched one, replaying TRANSIENT_LOCAL history, a service reply to that client included. At most RTPS_MAX_WAITING_MATCHES matches wait at once; a match that would wait beyond them is not recorded, while a match that can bind is always recorded.
